title: Armenian genocide
summary: On 24 April 1915 Ottoman authorities arrested 240 Armenian leaders in Constantinople and deported them east; Armenians commemorate this as the start of the genocide. The Ottoman government, controlled by the Committee of Union and Progress, directed the deportations and killings of Armenians. USHMM gives at least 664,000 and possibly as many as 1.2 million deaths; the Armenian National Institute says one and a half million perished between 1915 and 1923.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 24 April 1915 arrests in Constantinople (USHMM). The Armenian National Institute counts the genocide from 1915 to 1923; the Illinois Holocaust Museum gives 1915–1918 for the main phase.

as_recorded.value: arrest 240 Armenian leaders in Constantinople (today: Istanbul) on April 24, 1915
one and a half million Armenians perished between 1915 and 1923

when.display: From 24 April 1915 (Armenian National Institute counts to 1923)

where.modern_name: Istanbul, Turkey (site of the 24 April 1915 arrests; the deportations began mainly in six eastern provinces and ended in the Syrian desert regions)

importance.justification: A state-directed destruction of much of the Armenian population of the Ottoman Empire, condemned in 1915 by the international community (Armenian National Institute).

audience_note: This record concerns genocide: mass killing, deportation and starvation. Death-toll estimates vary by source (600,000 to 1.5 million) and the events are denied or disputed by the Turkish state.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about the Armenian Genocide

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin and counts: the pin is the 24 April arrests, not the whole genocide, which spanned Anatolia and the Syrian desert. Sources disagree on the arrests (USHMM 240 arrested; the Illinois museum says 235 killed) and on the toll (USHMM 664,000–1.2 million; ILHM 600,000–1.5 million; ANI 1.5 million). The Turkish state's position was not on an opened page.
